title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a connected, locally connected topos with a geometric point x0. Two contexts are allowed: discrete (X locally simply connected) or profinite (coverings are profinite coverings). A group Γ acts on X. Write π = π1(X, x0) and 𝓜 = π1(X, Γ; x0), the fundamental group of the 'quotient' (X, Γ), i.e. of the stack X/Γ. This gives an extension 1 → π → 𝓜 → Γ → 1. Grothendieck then fixes a Γ-stable abelian quotient M of π, equivalently of π_ab. Pushing out gives (presumably the extension numbered (287)) 1 → M → M̃ → Γ → 1, where M is abelian and Γ acts on it.

Problem studied on this page. He considers the Γ-equivariant coverings X' of (X, Γ) that, once the Γ-action is forgotten, are connected Galois coverings of X corresponding to the quotient M. Each such X' is naturally a torsor under the constant group M_X.

The fibre functor X' ↦ X'(x0) sends these objects to sets E with two structures.
(a) E is an M-torsor. Its affine group Aff(E) consists of the bijections of E that are semilinear with respect to some automorphism of M. It sits in an extension 1 → M → Aff(E) → Aut(M) → 1. Pulling back to Γ̃ = Im(Γ → Aut(M)) gives (288): 1 → M → Aff_Γ(E) → Γ̃ → 1.
(b) A morphism of extensions θ: M̃ → Aff_Γ(E), (289). It is the identity on M and the canonical map Γ → Γ̃ on quotients.

Claim: the category of such X' (with isomorphisms) is equivalent to the category of pairs (E, θ).

Check. Γ-equivariant coverings correspond to 𝓜-sets. Those whose underlying π-set is the M-Galois covering are exactly the 𝓜-sets that factor through M̃ and on which M acts simply transitively. If M̃ acts on an M-torsor E with M acting by translations, then each g ∈ M̃ acts by an affine map whose linear part is conjugation by g on M, i.e. the image of g in Γ̃ ⊂ Aut(M). Such actions are therefore the same as homomorphisms M̃ → Aff_Γ(E) over the identity of M. The claim is correct.

Where it leads (next page). Automorphisms of an object are translations by M^Γ. Isomorphism classes correspond to M-conjugacy classes of splittings of M̃ → Γ: the stabiliser in M̃ of a point e ∈ E is a complement to M. So the set of classes is either empty (obstruction in H²(Γ, M)) or a principal homogeneous space under H¹(Γ, M).

Purpose. This is the abelian case of the problem of descending / equivariantly lifting Galois coverings along a group action, e.g. Γ a Galois group acting on a geometric fundamental group. It is a step in the Longue Marche analysis of the extensions 1 → π → π1(X, Γ) → Γ → 1 and their sections.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor imprecision: in (a) the extension Aff(E) → Aut(M) is the full affine group; the restriction to Γ̃ is what matters. Note that Γ̃ may be a proper quotient of Γ, so θ need not be injective on the quotient.
The equivalence implicitly requires that the 𝓜-action on X'(x0) factor through M̃, i.e. that the kernel of π → M acts trivially. This is implicit in 'corresponding to the quotient M'.

ideas.what: Γ-equivariant connected abelian Galois coverings with group M are equivalent to M-torsors E with a morphism of extensions M̃ → Aff_Γ(E); equivalently, M̃-sets on which M acts simply transitively.
ideas.modern_name: Affine actions / descent of Galois covers; equivariant abelian covers via the pushout extension of the fundamental exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Galois descent; cf. field of moduli vs field of definition, Coombes–Harbater, Dèbes–Douai)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA1 exp. XIII-type exact sequences; the specific formulation is in the unpublished Longue Marche

ideas.what: Extension 1 → M → Aff(E) → Aut(M) → 1 and its pullback Aff_Γ(E) over Γ̃ = Im(Γ → Aut(M)).
ideas.modern_name: Holomorph / affine group of a torsor

ideas.what: (Continued next page) Isomorphism classes correspond to M-conjugacy classes of splittings of the abelianized extension, i.e. an H¹(Γ, M)-torsor with obstruction in H²(Γ, M); automorphisms are M^Γ.
ideas.modern_name: Splittings of group extensions with abelian kernel; abelianized section set

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard dictionary between equivariant abelian Galois coverings and splittings of the pushed-out fundamental extension. This is classical descent and extension theory, part of the systematic Longue Marche set-up, with nothing beyond the known record.
transcription_corrections: 'Π = Π_1(X, x0)' should read 'π = π_1(X, x0)', consistent with the previous page.
The marginal insertion reads roughly '{connexe ; (et galoisien)}' added above 'galoisien'; the extra '+étale+' is doubtful.
'et un tel que[?] tel donne naissance' is likely 'et un tel E donne naissance à une extension'.
Equation labels (288) and (289) were corrected in the manuscript (overwritten digits). The extension M̃ referred to on the next page as (287) is (**) on the previous page.
The last line reads 'un homom. d'extensions (289)'.
